summary: totp-utils postinstall exfiltrates Discord/Minecraft tokens and drops a JAR into Minecraft mods folders
details: Package advertised as a TOTP utility but ships an install-time and runtime credential stealer. package.json postinstall runs `node./index.js --setup`, which scans browser leveldb stores and Local State (including DPAPI-decrypted AES-256-GCM secrets) for Discord tokens and reads Minecraft launcher account files (Vanilla, Lunar, Modrinth) for access tokens, validates them against discord.com, and POSTs them to a hardcoded Discord webhook URL reassembled at runtime from a split base64 array (Buffer.from(_x.join(''), 'base64')). The same postinstall path downloads a JAR (optimized-renderer-1.0.0.jar) from a hardcoded Discord CDN attachments URL, also assembled from split base64 fragments, and writes it into detected Minecraft mods directories (.minecraft/mods, Modrinth profiles, Lunar offline versions), giving persistent code execution at Minecraft launch. The exported validateSecret() schedules _run() via setImmediate before returning, so any consumer importing totp-utils and calling the advertised TOTP API re-triggers the stealer and JAR drop at library-use time as well. Execution is explicitly skipped when CI, CONTINUOUS_INTEGRATION, JEST_WORKER_ID, or npm_config_global is set, indicating deliberate evasion of registry scanners and CI detonation environments.
